'''Easy Come, Easy Go Sealed Deck''' is a Star Wars CCG sealed-deck format in which every card that is lost, placed out of play or discarded is physically destroyed. [[Decipher]] ran it as a non-sanctioned side event at [[DecipherCon 2000]].<ref name="dcon-sw-events">[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/starwarsccg.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game events], DecipherCon 2000, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010126213800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/starwarsccg.html Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''Type:''' sealed deck
* '''Defined by:''' Decipher (2000)
* '''Card pool:''' 3 [[Premiere Unlimited|unlimited Premiere]] boosters, 2 Jabba's Palace boosters, and an [[Enhanced Premiere]] Darth Vader or Luke Skywalker pack per player
* '''In use:''' 2000 (DecipherCon 2000)
* '''Also called:''' Easy Come, Easy Go (Decipher's event page)
* '''GEMP:''' none

== Card pool ==
"Each player will be given 3 unlimited Premiere boosters, 2 Jabba's Palace boosters and either an EPP Darth Vader or EPP Luke Skywalker."<ref name="dcon-sw-events" />

Decipher's rules: "Whenever a card is lost, placed out of play or discarded, you must physically destroy it! Tear it in half, roll it into a ball, eat it - whatever! The catch: you must play with all of the cards that you are given, and if you drop early from the tournament, you must forfeit all of your cards."<ref name="dcon-sw-events" />

The page does not say whether players swap cards of the other side, as in a standard [[Sealed Deck]] event.

== History ==
Decipher scheduled one Star Wars event: Saturday 7 October 2000 at noon (event #SW232), single elimination, $10, non-sanctioned.<ref name="dcon-sw-events" /><ref name="dcon00-sched">[http://www2.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swccgevents.pdf DecipherCon Master Tournament Schedule for Decipher Games], DecipherCon 2000, Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030413152501/http://www2.decipher.com/tournaments/deciphercon2000/swccgevents.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> The same convention scheduled ''Star Trek'' CCG Easy Come, Easy Go sealed-deck events on 6 and 7 October.<ref name="dcon00-sched" />

The destroy rule had appeared a year earlier in [[Iron Man]], a constructed format at [[DecipherCon 1999]], with the same opening line: it "adds new meaning to the word 'lost'".<ref name="dc99-ironman">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/ironmanevents.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Descriptions: Iron-Man Events], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011005153720/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/ironmanevents.html Internet Archive].</ref>
